thread.title: How Apple’s latest iPhone update will improve health care for BayCare, Florida Hospital patients

author: Margie Manning
title: How Apple’s latest iPhone update will improve health care for BayCare, Florida Hospital patients
text: – Finance Editor, Tampa Bay Business Journal Mar 30, 2018, 7:24am EDT BayCare Health System and Adventist Health System, the parent company of Florida Hospital, are among the 39 health systems nationwide that are collaborating with Apple on a new way to access medical records. Test results and other personal health data can be tracked in an updated health records section that is included in the health app on the latest operating system from Apple (NASDAQ; AAPL), iOS 11.3, which was released Thursday. The tool is important, because patients who have access to their medical data are more involved in their own care, said Tim Thompson , senior vice president of information services for BayCare. “It really is about engagement, particularly for people with chronic conditions,” Thompson said. For instance, knowing lab outcomes can help patients make adjustments in their lifestyles, he said. In its own news release , Apple said the update means “doctors put patients in charge,” and that’s a big shift from the traditional way medicine has been practiced, CNBC reported , citing a 2015 report from the Alzheimer’s Association that found that just 45 percent of Medicare patients who’d been diagnosed with Alzheimer’s said they were informed of the diagnosis by their doctor. In addition, some hospitals still charge patients a fee to access their data, CNBC said. BayCare has made patient information available on its own app, the myBayCare patient portal, for several years. The Apple app doesn’t replicate everything that’s on the myBayCare app, Thompson said. “What it does include is lab results, procedures, medications, vitals and immunizations — those common things. You have the ability to download those from the BayCare app, and if you have a doctor who’s not a BayCare doctor but is connected to Apple, you’ll have that information too,” he said. One of the things Apple does well is making things easy for consumers, Thompson said. “Since we have our phone in our hands 20 hours a day, the information is at our fingertips. If you need it at the doctor’s office or the pharmacy, it’s another avenue to have that information,” he said. A patient can access Apple’s health records section from the health icon on their iPhone. Authentication is required the first time the patient uses it. The patient then clicks on the portal for their health care system and the information downloads automatically. Apple also has push notifications when new information is available. “As soon as your tests are back from the hospital, you know it on your phone,” Thompson said. The data is encrypted and protected with the patient’s iPhone passcode. Apple piloted the health records update with a dozen hospitals beginning in January. BayCare’s software vendor, Cerner , was part of the pilot, and worked with BayCare and Apple on the integration before Thursday’s launch, Thompson said. BayCare, with 15 hospitals and dozens of other facilities, is the largest nonprofit health care system in the Tampa Bay area. Florida Hospital, the West Florida Division of Adventist Health System, is a not-for-profit hospital system composed of nine hospitals and other facilities.
